guitar.notes: No iconic signature instrument well documented for Art Alexakis.

tone.target: dry mid-forward alt-rock crunch with slight fuzz edge
tone.profile: dry mid-forward alt-rock crunch with slight fuzz edge
tone.summary: Gate 1 -> Boost (OD 9) -> Distortion (RAT-style) -> UK 45 -> UK Vintage 4x12 -> Guitar EQ 1 -> Chorus -> Digital Delay -> Room

rig.name: Everclear - Father Of Mine - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and tighten the signal for palm-muted parts.
Simulate the Tube Screamer emphasis for mid-hump and attack boost.
blocks.gap: The GP-180 lacks a dedicated TS model, so Boost is used to achieve the mid-range focus and compression needed.

blocks.purpose: Provide the required 'slight fuzz edge' and aggressive crunch.
blocks.gap: RAT-style provides a gritty, mid-focused dirt that fits the alt-rock tone better than pure Distortion or Muff-style.

alternatives.model: Red Haze (if more psychedelic fuzz is needed)

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Marshall-style amp tone for classic alt-rock punch.

alternatives.model: UK 50 (if a slightly more open, British sound is preferred)

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British 4x12 cabinet sound.
Enhance the mid-forward crunch and cut any excessive low end.
Add subtle movement and width without sounding 'washy'.
blocks.gap: The instructions advise keeping effects minimal, but a slight Chorus adds necessary dimension for the genre.

blocks.purpose: Add space and definition to the rhythm parts.

blocks.gap: The goal is minimal effects, so the Room reverb is kept at a low mix.

alternatives.model: Plate (if a more controlled decay is preferred)

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and overall tone by swapping the default IR for a more aggressive, mid-focused alt-rock cab.

proposals.reason: Enhance the gritty, aggressive crunch required for Everclear's sound.
